Arm also signed one new CSS license for a data-center customer during the quarter, among three total new CSS licenses. [[3]]

tool_arguments.query: Arm Q1 fiscal 2026 data-center royalty revenue Neoverse CPU fiscal Q1 2026 ended June 2025

events.content: Arm Q1 fiscal 2026 data-center royalty revenue Neoverse CPU fiscal Q1 2026 ended June 2025

For Arm’s fiscal Q1 2026, ended June 30, 2025, the company did **not publicly disclose a standalone dollar amount for data-center royalty revenue or for Neoverse CPU royalties**; it reported only total royalty revenue of **$585 million**, up **25% year over year** from $467 million. [[1]] 

Management said the total royalty increase was driven by Armv9 adoption, the ramp of Arm Compute Subsystems (CSS), and greater deployment of Arm-based chips in data centers, while noting royalty growth across data center, automotive, smartphones, and IoT rather than providing an end-market revenue split. [[1]] 

As operating indicators for the data-center/Neoverse opportunity, Arm said it signed **two data-center CSS licenses** during the quarter, bringing total CSS licenses to **16 across 10 companies**, and estimated that at least **70,000 enterprises** were running data-center workloads on Arm Neoverse-based chips—a **14×** increase since 2021. [[2]] 

Thus, the supportable Q1 FY26 figure is **$585 million of company-wide royalty revenue**, not a separately reported Neoverse or data-center royalty-revenue number. [[1]]

events.content: Arm FY 2025 full year data-center royalty revenue Neoverse fiscal year ended March 2025

Arm’s fiscal 2025 ended March 31, 2025, with total revenue of **$4.007 billion**, up from **$3.233 billion** in fiscal 2024. [[1]]

- **Royalty revenue:** **$2.168 billion**, exceeding $2 billion for the first time and representing approximately **54.1%** of full-year revenue. [[2]] [[3]]
- **License and other revenue:** **$1.839 billion**, or approximately **45.9%** of total revenue. [[1]] [[3]]
- The implied year-over-year growth rates were approximately **21.8% for royalties** and **26.6% for license and other revenue**, based on FY2024 segment revenues of roughly $1.780 billion and $1.453 billion, respectively. [[1]] [[3]]

**Data-center / Neoverse read-through:** Arm did not disclose a separate full-year revenue figure specifically for data center or Neoverse in its FY2025 reporting. [[1]] [[2]] However, Arm explicitly identified increased usage of Arm-based chips in data centers as a driver of Q4 FY2025 royalty revenue, alongside Armv9 adoption and the ramp of Compute Subsystems (CSS). [[3]] In Q4, royalty revenue was **$607 million**, up **18% year over year**, while license-and-other revenue was **$634 million**, up **53% year over year**. [[3]] 

Neoverse was positioned as a key AI-data-center platform: Arm stated that the computational efficiency of its Neoverse platform was integral to AI data-center demand and noted that NVIDIA’s Armv9-based Grace Blackwell superchip had entered full production. [[2]] Arm also said FY2025 royalty growth came from all target end markets, specifically including data center, automotive, smartphones, and IoT. [[4]] 

The key analytical point is that **Neoverse/data-center exposure was an important qualitative royalty-growth driver in FY2025, but it was not separately quantified**; Arm’s reported economics remain the aggregate licensing plus per-chip royalty model. [[1]] [[3]]

private_messages.content:
Arm’s fiscal 2025 ended March 31, 2025, with total revenue of **$4.007 billion**, up from **$3.233 billion** in fiscal 2024. [[1]]

- **Royalty revenue:** **$2.168 billion**, exceeding $2 billion for the first time and representing approximately **54.1%** of full-year revenue. [[2]] [[3]]
- **License and other revenue:** **$1.839 billion**, or approximately **45.9%** of total revenue. [[1]] [[3]]
- The implied year-over-year growth rates were approximately **21.8% for royalties** and **26.6% for license and other revenue**, based on FY2024 segment revenues of roughly $1.780 billion and $1.453 billion, respectively. [[1]] [[3]]

**Data-center / Neoverse read-through:** Arm did not disclose a separate full-year revenue figure specifically for data center or Neoverse in its FY2025 reporting. [[1]] [[2]] However, Arm explicitly identified increased usage of Arm-based chips in data centers as a driver of Q4 FY2025 royalty revenue, alongside Armv9 adoption and the ramp of Compute Subsystems (CSS). [[3]] In Q4, royalty revenue was **$607 million**, up **18% year over year**, while license-and-other revenue was **$634 million**, up **53% year over year**. [[3]] 

Neoverse was positioned as a key AI-data-center platform: Arm stated that the computational efficiency of its Neoverse platform was integral to AI data-center demand and noted that NVIDIA’s Armv9-based Grace Blackwell superchip had entered full production. [[2]] Arm also said FY2025 royalty growth came from all target end markets, specifically including data center, automotive, smartphones, and IoT. [[4]] 

The key analytical point is that **Neoverse/data-center exposure was an important qualitative royalty-growth driver in FY2025, but it was not separately quantified**; Arm’s reported economics remain the aggregate licensing plus per-chip royalty model. [[1]] [[3]]

For Arm’s fiscal Q3 2026, ended December 31, 2025, total royalty revenue was a record **$737 million**, up **27% year over year** from $580 million. [[1]] 

Arm did **not disclose a dollar amount** for data-center royalty revenue; it reported that data-center royalty revenue grew at a **triple-digit year-over-year rate**. [[1]] 

The growth reflected increased deployment of Arm-based data-center chips as well as higher royalty rates from Armv9 and Compute Subsystems (CSS). [[1]] 

Arm also said its Neoverse CPUs had surpassed **1 billion cores deployed**, while it expected its share at top hyperscalers to approach **50%**. [[2]]
